subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Two's Complement: Negative Numbers in Binary
description: A quick win: understand Two's Complement: Negative Numbers in Binary.

hook.text: Binary has no minus sign. So how does a computer represent negative numbers?

buildup.text: Two's complement flips all bits and adds 1. The result represents the negative value.

discovery.text: In 8-bit two's complement, 11111111 is -1, not 255. The top bit signals the sign.

twist.text: Addition works the same for positive and negative — the hardware doesn't need a subtractor.

climax.text: Every processor uses two's complement for signed integers — it simplifies circuits enormously.

punchline.text: Flip the bits, add one — suddenly binary can go below zero.

quiz.question: Why is two's complement preferred for signed numbers?
options: It allows the same addition circuit to handle both positive and negative numbers
It doubles the range of representable numbers
It eliminates the need for binary altogether
